input.question: If f : {-1,1}^n -> [-1,1] has degree at most k, must there exist a coordinate i in [n] with influence Inf_i[f] >= (Var[f]/k)^{O(1)}?

original_question: If f : {-1,1}^n -> [-1,1] has degree at most k, must there exist a coordinate i in [n] with influence Inf_i[f] >= (Var[f]/k)^{O(1)}?

original_paper.title: Open Problems in Analysis of Boolean Functions

rewritten_question: Let f be a function on the discrete cube {−1,1}^n with values in [−1,1], and suppose f is represented by a real polynomial of total degree at most k. For a coordinate i, let Inf_i[f] denote the influence of the i-th coordinate, meaning the expected squared change in f when the i-th input bit is flipped, and let Var[f] denote the variance of f under the uniform distribution on the cube. Must there always exist some coordinate i such that Inf_i[f] is at least a fixed polynomial in Var[f]/k; equivalently, is there a universal constant c > 0 for which Inf_i[f] ≥ (Var[f]/k)^c for some i?

paper_evidence.quote: Aaronson–Ambainis Conjecture Statement: Let f : {−1,1}^n → [−1,1] have degree at most k. Then there exists i ∈ [n] with Infi[f] ≥ (Var[f]/k)^{O(1)}.

Remarks: • True for f : {−1,1}^n → {−1,1}; this follows from a result of O’Donnell, Schramm, Saks, and Servedio [OSSS05]. • The weaker lower bound (Var[f]/2^k)^{O(1)} follows from a result of Dinur, Kindler, Friedgut, and O’Donnell [DFKO07].

Conjecture 6 (Bounded Polynomials Have Influential Variables) Let p : R^N → R be a polynomial of degree d. Suppose that 0 ≤ p(X) ≤ 1 for all X ∈ {0, 1}^N, and E_X[(p(X) − E[p])^2] ≥ ε. Then there exists an i such that Infi[p] ≥ (ε/d)^{O(1)}.

Recall Conjecture 6, which said that bounded polynomials have influential variables: that is, for every degree-d polynomial p : R^N → R such that 0 ≤ p(X) ≤ 1 for all X ∈ {0, 1}^N, there exists an i ∈ [N] such that Infi[p] ≥ (Var [p] /d)^{O(1)}, where Infi[p] := E_X[(p(X) − p(X^i))^2], Var [p] := E_X[(p(X) − E [p])^2].

The Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture (Theory of Computing ’14) says that every low-degree bounded polynomial on the Boolean hypercube has an influential variable. ... We prove a special case of the conjecture: in every completely bounded degree-d block-multilinear form with constant variance, there always exists a variable with influence at least 1/poly(d).

Conjecture 1.2 (Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture). Let f : {±1}^n → [0, 1] be a degree-d multilinear polynomial. Then, the maximum influence among all variables in f is at least poly(Var[f], 1/d). The above conjecture poses a fundamental structural question about bounded polynomials on the hypercube and is a notable open problem in the analysis of Boolean functions.

One of the central open problems in the field of quantum query complexity is ... Aaronson and Ambainis proposed the following conjecture: let f : {±1}^n → [0, 1] be a degree d polynomial with variance ≥ ϵ. Then, there exists a coordinate of f with influence ≥ poly(ϵ, 1/d).

We show that for any polynomial f : {±1}^n → [0, 1] of degree d (d ≥ 2) and variance Var[f] ≥ 1/d, if ρ denotes a random restriction ... Thus, Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture is true for a non-negligible fraction of random restrictions of the given polynomial assuming its variance is not too low.
